problem: Existing embodied frameworks split data collection, policy learning and deployment into disjoint stages, lack explicit physical constraints, and bind high-level LLM planners to fragmented robot SDKs. This makes long-horizon multi-policy execution on heterogeneous robots fragile and costly to port.
motivation: LLMs reason well semantically but lack grounded knowledge of physical dynamics and timing. Heterogeneous hardware with non-standard SDKs blocks unified coordination, and open-loop pipelines never turn physical interaction into reusable knowledge. The paper aims for a closed loop that links semantic reasoning, physical safety checks and data accumulation.
key_idea: A three-layer semantic-physical agent framework (cognitive VLM/LLM, OpenClaw coordination with an Online Tool Pool and an e-URDF digital-twin physical firewall, and a physical layer with a Local Resource Pool) that decouples low-frequency reasoning from high-frequency control and feeds execution data back to the agent.
insight: The paper argues that pre-execution physical validation (forward dynamics and collision checks with e-URDF in Isaac Lab) plus a unified tool abstraction lets an LLM agent orchestrate heterogeneous robots safely with little human effort. The only evidence is qualitative real-world demos and a claim of about 3 minutes to generate a 7-gimbal dance. No ablations or baselines quantify the contribution of any component.
method: Three-layer architecture: information space (cognitive layer), software system (coordination automation layer) and physical world, with asynchronous decoupling of low-frequency semantic planning from high-frequency control.
Cognitive layer: LLM/VLM that decomposes tasks, reasons over long horizons and receives execution feedback bidirectionally.

Online Tool Pool (OpenClaw-centered): aggregates robot SDKs, MCP services and APIs (e.g. DINO-X, VLM, music generation) as a 'digital dictionary' mapping abstract instructions to concrete software calls.
e-URDF physical firewall: a headless Isaac Lab digital twin runs forward dynamics, collision detection and joint torque validation on e-URDF models, filtering infeasible commands before dispatch.
ROSClaw physical world: ROS and drivers give unified control of heterogeneous agents while sensing physical states at high frequency.

Local Resource Pool / data collection and state accumulation: stores robot states, multimodal observations and successful trajectories as reusable skills. It can be uploaded for cloud fine-tuning and fed back to the cognitive layer.
Task Execution Supervision (TES) and multi-objective scheduling: mentioned for task assignment by robot-accessible regions, but not described in detail.

setting.backbone: Unspecified LLM/VLM in the OpenClaw agent (frozen, API-based); DINO-X API for grasp candidates
setting.training_data: none (no training reported; the framework only accumulates data for future use)
setting.observation: RealSense RGB camera, humanoid head-mounted camera, robot joint states
setting.action_space: Tool/SDK-level calls to robot APIs via MCP/ROS (e.g. navigation, grasping, door opening, gimbal motion)
setting.simulator: Isaac Lab (digital twin for validation); real world for demos
setting.privileged: none stated (e-URDF robot models and known region/accessibility constraints per robot)

numbers_note: No quantitative benchmark results; only qualitative real-world demos and an unquantified claim of about 3 minutes to generate the multi-gimbal dance.
results: Real-world demos show a mobile manipulator, a humanoid and a fixed arm collaborating on a fruit-transport task in a roughly 60 m^2 smart home. Seven gimbals were also orchestrated in a dance with e-URDF safety checks in about three minutes. No baselines, success rates or ablations are reported.
limitations: Purely qualitative validation with no benchmarks, metrics, baselines or ablations.
Evaluated only in structured or semi-dynamic environments, with no handling of disturbances or perception noise.
The Local Resource Pool does not yet form a closed-loop learning system that optimizes policies autonomously.
